source.text: Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν θησαυρῷ κεκρυμμένῳ ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ, ὃν εὑρὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔκρυψεν, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς αὐτοῦ ὑπάγει καὶ πωλεῖ πάντα ὅσα ἔχει καὶ ἀγοράζει τὸν ἀγρὸν ἐκεῖνον.

records.literal_gloss: Like is the kingdom of the heavens to treasure having been hidden in the field, which having found a man hid, and from the joy of him he goes and sells all as much as he has and buys the field that.

en.L: The kingdom of the heavens is like treasure hidden in the field, which a man found and hid; and in his joy he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.
en.B: The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure buried in a field. A man came across it and covered it up again. Then, full of joy, he went and sold everything he owned and bought that field.
en.R: The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure that was hidden in a field. One day a man found it, and he hid it again. He was filled with joy. So he went and sold everything he owned, and he bought that field.

es.L: El reino de los cielos es semejante a un tesoro escondido en el campo, que un hombre encontró y escondió; y por su alegría va y vende todo cuanto tiene y compra aquel campo.
es.B: El reino de los cielos es como un tesoro enterrado en un campo. Un hombre dio con él y volvió a taparlo. Luego, lleno de alegría, fue a vender todo lo que poseía y compró ese campo.
es.R: El reino de los cielos es como un tesoro que estaba escondido en un campo. Un día, un hombre lo encontró y lo volvió a esconder. Se llenó de alegría. Entonces fue y vendió todo lo que tenía, y compró ese campo.

fr.L: Le royaume des cieux est semblable à un trésor caché dans le champ, qu’un homme a trouvé et qu’il a caché ; et dans sa joie, il s’en va, il vend tout ce qu’il a et il achète ce champ-là.
fr.B: Le royaume des cieux est semblable à un trésor enfoui dans un champ. Un homme l’a découvert et l’a recouvert. Puis, rempli de joie, il est allé vendre tout ce qu’il possédait, et il a acheté ce champ.
fr.R: Le royaume des cieux ressemble à un trésor qui était caché dans un champ. Un jour, un homme l’a trouvé, et il l’a caché de nouveau. Il était plein de joie. Alors il est allé vendre tout ce qu’il avait, et il a acheté ce champ.

sw.L: Ufalme wa mbinguni unafanana na hazina iliyofichwa shambani, ambayo mtu aliiona akaificha; na kwa sababu ya furaha yake anakwenda na kuuza kila kitu alicho nacho na kulinunua shamba lile.
sw.B: Ufalme wa mbinguni ni kama hazina iliyozikwa shambani. Mtu mmoja aliigundua, akaifunika tena. Kisha, akiwa amejaa furaha, akaenda akauza mali yake yote, akalinunua shamba lile.
sw.R: Ufalme wa mbinguni ni kama hazina iliyokuwa imefichwa shambani. Siku moja mtu aliiona, akaificha tena. Akajaa furaha. Basi akaenda akauza kila kitu alichokuwa nacho, akalinunua shamba lile.

vi.L: Vương quốc thiên đàng giống như của báu chôn giấu trong ruộng, mà một người tìm thấy thì giấu đi; rồi vì vui mừng, người ấy đi bán hết mọi thứ mình có và mua thửa ruộng ấy.
vi.B: Vương quốc thiên đàng giống như một kho báu chôn giấu trong ruộng. Có người tình cờ tìm thấy, liền lấp lại. Rồi đầy vui mừng, người ấy đi bán hết mọi thứ mình có mà mua thửa ruộng ấy.
vi.R: Vương quốc thiên đàng giống như một kho báu được giấu trong ruộng. Một ngày kia, có một người tìm thấy kho báu ấy, rồi người ấy giấu nó lại. Người ấy rất vui mừng. Vì vậy, người ấy đi bán hết mọi thứ mình có và mua thửa ruộng đó.

ko.L: 천국은 밭에 숨겨진 보물과 같다. 어떤 사람이 그것을 발견하고 숨겨 두었다. 그리고 그 기쁨 때문에 가서 자기가 가진 것을 모두 팔아 그 밭을 산다.
ko.B: 천국은 밭에 묻혀 있는 보물과 같다. 어떤 사람이 그 보물을 발견하고 다시 묻어 두었다. 그러고는 기쁨에 넘쳐 가서 가진 것을 다 팔아 그 밭을 샀다.
ko.R: 천국은 밭에 숨겨져 있는 보물과 같다. 어느 날 한 사람이 그 보물을 찾아냈다. 그는 그것을 다시 숨겨 두었다. 그는 기쁨이 넘쳤다. 그래서 가서 자기가 가진 것을 모두 팔아 그 밭을 샀다.

pt.L: O Reino dos céus é semelhante a um tesouro escondido no campo, que um homem achou e escondeu; e, pela alegria [que sente], vai, vende tudo o que tem e compra aquele campo.
pt.B: O Reino dos céus é como um tesouro enterrado num campo. Um homem o encontrou e o escondeu de novo. Então, cheio de alegria, foi, vendeu tudo o que tinha e comprou aquele campo.
pt.R: O Reino dos céus é como um tesouro que estava escondido num campo. Um dia, um homem o encontrou e o escondeu de novo. Ele ficou muito alegre. Então foi, vendeu tudo o que tinha e comprou aquele campo.

decisions.choice: treasure hidden in a field: valuables buried for safekeeping
alternatives: a treasure placed there for him
decisions.reason: With no banks, people buried money and jewels, especially in time of war, and some was never recovered.

decisions.choice: in his joy: his joy is the reason he sells everything
decisions.reason: "His" refers to the man. Giving up everything is not a loss to him; it comes from his joy.

decisions.choice: the point is the worth of the kingdom, not the man's conduct
decisions.reason: The parable does not judge whether he should have told the owner. It shows that the kingdom is worth everything a person has.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: a man, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The man who finds the treasure is a figure in a parable, so the pronouns for him take no deity_pronoun span, as with the bridegroom at 9:15.

decisions.choice: el reino de los cielos (every level)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts for Matthew's phrase. Spanish says "los cielos" in the plural naturally, so every level keeps the Greek plural, where English changes to "heaven" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: va, vende, compra (L); fue, vendió, compró (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the present of the Greek story; Balanced and Readable tell it in the past, as Spanish narrative does.

decisions.choice: the parables in the passé composé at every level; Matthew's presents of narration kept at Literal ("il s’en va, il vend")
decisions.reason: The parables are Jesus's speech, so their past events are in the passé composé at every level, as in 13:24-33 and Mark 4 (style guide section 9). Literal keeps the presents the Greek uses for the man's actions, as English Literal does.

decisions.choice: "le royaume des cieux" at every level
decisions.reason: The New Testament term sheet, as in 13:24.

decisions.choice: ufalme wa mbinguni (every level)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts for Matthew's phrase. "Mbinguni" (in heaven) is the natural Swahili form and stands for the Greek plural "the heavens" at every level.

decisions.choice: anakwenda, kuuza, kulinunua (L); akaenda, akauza, akalinunua (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the present of the Greek story; Balanced and Readable tell it in the narrative past, with -ka- for the verbs that follow.

decisions.choice: "đi bán ... và mua" with no "đã" (L)
decisions.reason: Matthew tells the man's actions in the present ("goes", "sells", "buys"); Literal keeps that by leaving out "đã". A figure in the story, so no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: "kho báu" (B, R); "của báu" (L)
decisions.reason: Valuables buried for safekeeping (meaning decision); "kho báu" is the everyday word for a buried treasure.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Matthew 13:44-58; "천국" at every level; historic presents kept only at Literal ("산다", "말한다")
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so respect for Jesus is carried by -시-, 께서 and 그분 (docs/korean-style.md sections 4 and 7). Literal keeps Matthew's present of narration, as the Korean Matthew does through chapters 2-13.

decisions.choice: "기쁨" at every level
decisions.reason: Joy is a key term; Korean keeps the noun at every level, as the Korean Mark 4:16 does. His joy is the reason he sells everything (meaning decision).

source.text: Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ ἐμπόρῳ ζητοῦντι καλοὺς μαργαρίτας·

records.literal_gloss: Again like is the kingdom of the heavens to a man merchant seeking fine pearls;

en.L: Again, the kingdom of the heavens is like a merchant seeking fine pearls;
en.B: Or again, the kingdom of heaven is like a trader who was searching for fine pearls.
en.R: Here is another picture of the kingdom of heaven. A merchant was looking for fine pearls.

es.L: Otra vez, el reino de los cielos es semejante a un mercader que busca perlas finas;
es.B: Además, el reino de los cielos es como un comerciante que andaba buscando perlas finas.
es.R: Esta es otra imagen del reino de los cielos. Un comerciante buscaba perlas finas.

fr.L: De nouveau, le royaume des cieux est semblable à un marchand qui cherchait de belles perles ;
fr.B: Ou encore, le royaume des cieux est semblable à un négociant qui était à la recherche de belles perles.
fr.R: Voici encore une image du royaume des cieux. Un marchand cherchait de belles perles.

sw.L: Tena, ufalme wa mbinguni unafanana na mtu mfanyabiashara anayetafuta lulu nzuri;
sw.B: Au tena, ufalme wa mbinguni ni kama mfanyabiashara aliyekuwa akitafuta lulu za thamani.
sw.R: Huu ni mfano mwingine wa ufalme wa mbinguni. Mfanyabiashara mmoja alikuwa akitafuta lulu nzuri.

vi.L: Lại nữa, vương quốc thiên đàng giống như một thương gia đi tìm ngọc trai quý;
vi.B: Lại nữa, vương quốc thiên đàng giống như một thương gia đang tìm mua những viên ngọc trai đẹp.
vi.R: Đây là một hình ảnh khác về vương quốc thiên đàng. Có một người buôn bán đang đi tìm những viên ngọc trai quý.

ko.L: 또 천국은 좋은 진주들을 찾는 상인과 같다.
ko.B: 또 천국은 좋은 진주를 찾아다니는 상인과 같다.
ko.R: 천국은 또 이런 일과 같다. 어떤 상인이 좋은 진주를 찾아다니고 있었다.

pt.L: De novo, o Reino dos céus é semelhante a um negociante que procura pérolas finas;
pt.B: O Reino dos céus é também como um comerciante que procurava pérolas finas.
pt.R: Aqui está outra comparação para o Reino dos céus. Um comerciante procurava pérolas bonitas.

decisions.choice: a merchant seeking fine pearls: a wholesale dealer who traveled to buy
decisions.reason: The word means a trader who travels. Pearls came from the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea and were among the most valued of jewels.

decisions.choice: the kingdom is like a merchant: like what happens in his story
decisions.reason: As in 13:24, the comparison is with the story as a whole.

decisions.choice: a merchant
decisions.reason: The Greek says "a man, a merchant", a way of saying "a merchant".

decisions.choice: "thương gia" (L, B); "người buôn bán" (R)
decisions.reason: A dealer who travelled to buy (meaning decision); "thương gia" is the standard word, and Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: "천국은 또 이런 일과 같다" (R)
decisions.reason: The kingdom is like what happens in the merchant's story (meaning decision); Readable says so first and then tells it, as the English Readable does.

source.text: εὑρὼν δὲ ἕνα πολύτιμον μαργαρίτην ἀπελθὼν πέπρακεν πάντα ὅσα εἶχεν καὶ ἠγόρασεν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: having found but one very precious pearl having gone away has sold all as much as he had and bought it.

en.L: and having found one very valuable pearl, he went away and sold all that he had and bought it.
en.B: When he came upon a single pearl of very high price, he went and sold off all his possessions and bought it.
en.R: He found one pearl that was worth a great deal. So he went and sold everything he had, and he bought that pearl.

es.L: y, habiendo encontrado una perla de mucho valor, se fue, vendió todo cuanto tenía y la compró.
es.B: Cuando halló una perla de altísimo precio, fue, vendió todas sus posesiones y la compró.
es.R: Encontró una perla que valía muchísimo. Entonces fue y vendió todo lo que tenía, y compró esa perla.

fr.L: et ayant trouvé une perle de grande valeur, il s’en est allé, il a vendu tout ce qu’il avait et il l’a achetée.
fr.B: Quand il a découvert une perle d’un très grand prix, il est allé vendre tous ses biens et il l’a achetée.
fr.R: Il a trouvé une perle qui valait très cher. Alors il est allé vendre tout ce qu’il avait, et il a acheté cette perle.

sw.L: na alipoipata lulu moja yenye thamani kubwa sana, akaenda zake, akauza kila kitu alichokuwa nacho, akainunua.
sw.B: Alipogundua lulu moja ya bei kubwa mno, alikwenda akauza mali yake yote, akainunua.
sw.R: Akaipata lulu moja yenye thamani kubwa sana. Basi akaenda akauza kila kitu alichokuwa nacho, akainunua lulu ile.

vi.L: và khi tìm được một viên ngọc trai rất quý giá, người ấy đi bán hết mọi thứ mình có và mua viên ngọc ấy.
vi.B: Khi tìm được một viên ngọc trai vô cùng quý giá, người ấy liền đi bán sạch mọi tài sản mình có mà mua viên ngọc ấy.
vi.R: Người ấy tìm được một viên ngọc trai rất có giá trị. Vì vậy, người ấy đi bán hết mọi thứ mình có và mua viên ngọc trai đó.

ko.L: 그러다가 아주 값진 진주 하나를 발견하자, 가서 가진 것을 모두 팔아 버리고 그것을 샀다.
ko.B: 그러다가 아주 값진 진주 하나를 발견하자, 가서 가진 것을 모두 팔아 그 진주를 샀다.
ko.R: 그러다가 아주 비싼 진주 하나를 찾아냈다. 그래서 그는 가서 자기가 가진 것을 모두 팔았다. 그리고 그 진주를 샀다.

pt.L: e, tendo encontrado uma pérola de grande valor, foi, vendeu tudo o que tinha e a comprou.
pt.B: Quando encontrou uma única pérola de altíssimo valor, foi, vendeu todos os seus bens e a comprou.
pt.R: Ele encontrou uma pérola que valia muito dinheiro. Então foi, vendeu tudo o que tinha e comprou aquela pérola.

decisions.choice: sold: the perfect tense, a decisive and complete sale
decisions.reason: The tense stresses that the sale was made and done. He kept nothing back.

decisions.choice: selling everything: the kingdom is worth more than all else
decisions.reason: The point, as in 13:44, is the surpassing worth of the kingdom (compare 19:21, 29).

decisions.choice: "liền ... bán sạch" (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek perfect marks a decisive, complete sale (meaning decision); Balanced shows that with "liền" and "sạch".

decisions.choice: "팔아 버리다" (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek perfect marks a decisive and complete sale (meaning decision); Literal shows it with "-아 버리다".

source.text: Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν σαγήνῃ βληθείσῃ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ ἐκ παντὸς γένους συναγαγούσῃ·

records.literal_gloss: Again like is the kingdom of the heavens to a dragnet having been cast into the sea and from every kind having gathered;

en.L: Again, the kingdom of the heavens is like a dragnet that was cast into the sea and gathered [fish] of every kind;
en.B: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a dragnet that was let down into the lake and pulled in fish of every kind.
en.R: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a big fishing net. People put it into the lake, and it caught all kinds of fish.

es.L: Otra vez, el reino de los cielos es semejante a una red barredera echada al mar, que recogió [peces] de toda clase;
es.B: Además, el reino de los cielos es como una red barredera que se echó en el lago y recogió peces de toda clase.
es.R: El reino de los cielos es también como una gran red de pesca. La echaron al lago y atrapó toda clase de peces.

fr.L: De nouveau, le royaume des cieux est semblable à un filet qu’on a jeté dans la mer et qui a ramassé [des poissons] de toute espèce ;
fr.B: Le royaume des cieux est encore semblable à un grand filet qu’on a descendu dans le lac et qui a ramené des poissons de toute sorte.
fr.R: Le royaume des cieux ressemble aussi à un grand filet de pêche. Des gens l’ont mis dans le lac, et il a attrapé toutes sortes de poissons.

sw.L: Tena, ufalme wa mbinguni unafanana na juya lililotupwa baharini na kukusanya [samaki] wa kila aina;
sw.B: Tena, ufalme wa mbinguni ni kama juya lililoshushwa ziwani, likavua samaki wa kila aina.
sw.R: Tena, ufalme wa mbinguni ni kama wavu mkubwa wa kuvulia samaki. Watu waliutupa ziwani, nao ukanasa samaki wa kila aina.

vi.L: Lại nữa, vương quốc thiên đàng giống như một tấm lưới kéo được thả xuống biển và gom được [cá] đủ loại;
vi.B: Lại nữa, vương quốc thiên đàng giống như một tấm lưới kéo được thả xuống biển và bắt được đủ loại cá.
vi.R: Vương quốc thiên đàng cũng giống như một tấm lưới đánh cá lớn. Người ta thả lưới xuống hồ, và lưới bắt được đủ thứ cá.

ko.L: 또 천국은 바다에 던져져서 온갖 종류의 [물고기를] 모아들인 끌그물과 같다.
ko.B: 또 천국은 바다에 쳐서 온갖 물고기를 끌어모은 그물과 같다.
ko.R: 또 천국은 커다란 그물과 같다. 사람들이 그 그물을 호수에 던졌더니, 온갖 물고기가 잡혔다.

pt.L: De novo, o Reino dos céus é semelhante a uma rede de arrasto lançada ao mar, que recolheu [peixes] de toda espécie;
pt.B: O Reino dos céus é também como uma rede de arrasto que foi lançada no lago e apanhou peixes de todo tipo.
pt.R: O Reino dos céus é também como uma grande rede de pesca. Jogaram a rede no lago, e ela pegou todo tipo de peixe.

decisions.choice: a dragnet: a long net with floats on top and weights below, drawn to shore
decisions.reason: Boats or men on the shore dragged it through the water, and it caught everything in its path. It is a different word from the net of 4:18.

decisions.choice: of every kind: fish of every kind, good and bad
decisions.reason: The parable speaks of fish. The application comes in 13:49.

decisions.choice: the lake (B, R); the sea (L)
decisions.reason: As at 13:1.

decisions.choice: una red barredera (L, B); una gran red de pesca (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word names a long net drawn through the water to the shore (meaning decision m1). "Red barredera" is that net; Readable describes it in plain words.

decisions.choice: el mar (L); el lago (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps "mar", the Greek word; Balanced and Readable say "lago", since the Sea of Galilee is a lake.

decisions.choice: juya (L, B); wavu mkubwa wa kuvulia samaki (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word names a long net drawn through the water to the shore (meaning decision m1). "Juya" is the Swahili name for that seine net; "wavu" is any net, so Readable adds "mkubwa" and says what it was for.

decisions.choice: baharini (L); ziwani (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps "bahari", the Greek word; Balanced and Readable say "ziwa", since the Sea of Galilee is a lake.

decisions.choice: "lưới kéo" (L, B); "lưới đánh cá lớn" (R)
decisions.reason: A long net drawn to shore (meaning decision); "lưới kéo" says how it is used.

decisions.choice: "biển" (L, B); "hồ" (R)
decisions.reason: As in 13:1: Literal and Balanced keep Matthew's word; Readable says it is a lake.

decisions.choice: "끌그물" (L), "그물" (B), "커다란 그물" (R); "바다" (L, B), "호수" (R)
decisions.reason: A dragnet is drawn to shore (meaning decision); Literal names the kind, the others keep the plain word. The sea is worded as in 13:1.

source.text: ἣν ὅτε ἐπληρώθη ἀναβιβάσαντες ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν καὶ καθίσαντες συνέλεξαν τὰ καλὰ εἰς ἄγγη, τὰ δὲ σαπρὰ ἔξω ἔβαλον.

records.literal_gloss: which when it was filled having drawn up onto the shore and having sat down they gathered the good into vessels, the but bad out they threw.

en.L: which, when it was full, they drew up onto the shore, and sitting down, they gathered the good into containers, but threw the bad out.
en.B: When it was full, they hauled it onto the beach, sat down, and sorted the good fish into baskets, while the worthless ones they threw away.
en.R: When the net was full, the fishermen pulled it up on the shore. They sat down and sorted the fish. They put the good fish into baskets. But they threw away the bad fish.

es.L: la cual, cuando se llenó, la sacaron a la orilla, y sentándose, recogieron los buenos en recipientes, pero a los malos los echaron fuera.
es.B: Cuando estuvo llena, la arrastraron hasta la playa, se sentaron y pusieron los peces buenos en cestas, mientras que los que no servían los tiraron.
es.R: Cuando la red estuvo llena, los pescadores la sacaron a la orilla. Se sentaron y separaron los peces. Pusieron los buenos en cestas. Pero tiraron los malos.

fr.L: Quand il a été plein, ils l’ont tiré sur le rivage, et s’étant assis, ils ont ramassé les bons dans des récipients, mais ils ont jeté dehors les mauvais.
fr.B: Quand il a été plein, ils l’ont tiré sur la plage, ils se sont assis et ils ont trié les bons poissons dans des paniers, tandis que les mauvais, ils les ont jetés.
fr.R: Quand le filet a été plein, les pêcheurs l’ont tiré sur le rivage. Ils se sont assis et ils ont trié les poissons. Ils ont mis les bons poissons dans des paniers. Mais ils ont jeté les mauvais.

sw.L: ambalo lilipojaa, wakalivuta pwani, na wakiisha kuketi, wakawakusanya wazuri katika vyombo, lakini wabaya wakawatupa nje.
sw.B: Lilipojaa, walilivuta mpaka ufuoni, wakaketi, wakawachagua samaki wazuri na kuwaweka katika vikapu, lakini wale wasiofaa wakawatupa.
sw.R: Wavu ulipojaa, wavuvi waliuvuta mpaka ufuoni. Wakaketi, wakawachambua samaki. Wakawaweka samaki wazuri katika vikapu. Lakini samaki wabaya wakawatupa.

vi.L: Khi lưới đã đầy, người ta kéo lên bờ, rồi ngồi xuống, gom những con tốt vào thùng, còn những con xấu thì ném ra ngoài.
vi.B: Khi lưới đầy, người ta kéo lên bờ, ngồi xuống lựa cá tốt bỏ vào giỏ, còn cá xấu thì vứt đi.
vi.R: Khi lưới đầy cá, những người đánh cá kéo lưới lên bờ. Họ ngồi xuống và lựa cá. Họ bỏ cá tốt vào giỏ, nhưng vứt bỏ những con cá không ăn được.

ko.L: 그물이 가득 차자 [사람들이] 물가로 끌어 올리고 앉아서, 좋은 것들은 그릇에 모아 담고 나쁜 것들은 밖으로 내던졌다.
ko.B: 그물이 가득 차자 사람들은 그것을 물가로 끌어 올리고 앉아서, 좋은 물고기는 바구니에 골라 담고 못 쓸 것은 내버렸다.
ko.R: 그물이 가득 차자 어부들이 그물을 물가로 끌어 올렸다. 그들은 앉아서 물고기를 골랐다. 좋은 물고기는 바구니에 담았다. 그러나 나쁜 물고기는 내버렸다.

pt.L: a qual, quando ficou cheia, puxaram para a praia e, sentando-se, recolheram os bons em vasilhas, mas jogaram fora os ruins.
pt.B: Quando ficou cheia, eles a puxaram para a praia, sentaram-se e separaram os peixes bons em cestos, e os que não prestavam jogaram fora.
pt.R: Quando a rede ficou cheia, os pescadores a puxaram para a praia. Eles se sentaram e separaram os peixes. Puseram os peixes bons em cestos. Mas jogaram fora os peixes ruins.

decisions.choice: the bad: fish that could not be eaten or sold
decisions.reason: The word means rotten or worthless. Some fish were unclean under the law, having no fins or scales (Leviticus 11:9-12), and some were simply useless.

decisions.choice: containers: vessels or baskets for the catch
decisions.reason: The word means any container.

decisions.choice: the fishermen
decisions.reason: Readable says who drew up the net.

decisions.choice: "thùng" (L); "giỏ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Vessels or baskets for the catch (meaning decision); "giỏ" is the basket a Vietnamese fisher uses.

decisions.choice: "[사람들이]" (L), "사람들" (B), "어부들" (R); "그릇" (L), "바구니" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Korean needs the subject the Greek leaves to be understood; Readable names the fishermen, as the English Readable does. The containers were vessels or baskets (meaning decision).

source.text: οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ αἰῶνος· ἐξελεύσονται οἱ ἄγγελοι καὶ ἀφοριοῦσιν τοὺς πονηροὺς ἐκ μέσου τῶν δικαίων καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.

records.literal_gloss: So it will be in the consummation of the age; will come out the angels and will separate the evil from middle of the righteous \v 50 and will throw them into the furnace of the fire; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of the teeth.

en.L: So it will be at the end of the age: the angels will go out and separate the evil from among the righteous \v 50 and will throw them into the furnace of fire; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
en.B: The end of the age will be like this. The angels will go out and remove the wicked from among the righteous, \v 50 and they will throw them into the burning furnace. There people will weep and grind their teeth.
en.R: That is how it will be at the end of the world. The angels will come and take the evil people away from the people who do what God wants. \v 50 The angels will throw the evil people into the fire that burns like a furnace. There they will cry and grind their teeth.

es.L: Así será en la consumación de la era: saldrán los ángeles y separarán a los malos de en medio de los justos \v 50 y los arrojarán al horno de fuego; allí será el llanto y el rechinar de los dientes.
es.B: Así será el fin de la era. Los ángeles saldrán y apartarán a los malvados de entre los justos, \v 50 y los arrojarán al horno encendido. Allí la gente llorará y rechinará los dientes.
es.R: Así sucederá al fin del mundo. Los ángeles vendrán y separarán a la gente mala de los que hacen lo que Dios quiere. \v 50 Los ángeles echarán a la gente mala en el fuego que arde como un horno. Allí llorarán y harán rechinar los dientes.

fr.L: Ainsi en sera-t-il à la fin de l’âge : les anges sortiront et sépareront les méchants du milieu des justes \v 50 et ils les jetteront dans la fournaise de feu ; là il y aura les pleurs et le grincement des dents.
fr.B: Il en sera ainsi à la fin de l’âge présent. Les anges viendront et retireront les méchants du milieu des justes, \v 50 et ils les jetteront dans la fournaise ardente. Là, on pleurera et on grincera des dents.
fr.R: C’est ce qui se passera à la fin du monde. Les anges viendront et ils sépareront les méchants des gens qui font ce que Dieu veut. \v 50 Les anges jetteront les méchants dans le feu qui brûle comme un four. Là, ils pleureront et ils grinceront des dents.

sw.L: Ndivyo itakavyokuwa katika utimilifu wa enzi: malaika watatoka na kuwatenga waovu kutoka kati ya wenye haki \v 50 na kuwatupa katika tanuru la moto; huko kutakuwa na kilio na kusaga kwa meno.
sw.B: Mwisho wa enzi utakuwa hivi. Malaika watatoka na kuwaondoa waovu kutoka kati ya wenye haki, \v 50 nao watawatupa katika tanuru linalowaka moto. Huko watu watalia na kusaga meno yao.
sw.R: Ndivyo itakavyokuwa mwisho wa dunia. Malaika watakuja na kuwaondoa watu waovu kutoka kati ya watu wanaofanya yale Mungu anayotaka. \v 50 Malaika watawatupa watu waovu katika moto unaowaka kama tanuru. Huko watalia na kusaga meno yao.

vi.L: Vào lúc kết thúc của đời này cũng sẽ như vậy: các thiên sứ sẽ đi ra và tách những kẻ ác ra khỏi những người công chính, \v 50 và sẽ quăng chúng vào lò lửa; ở đó sẽ có khóc lóc và nghiến răng.
vi.B: Lúc kết thúc của đời này cũng sẽ như vậy. Các thiên sứ sẽ đi ra, tách những kẻ gian ác ra khỏi những người công chính, \v 50 và quăng chúng vào lò lửa, là nơi người ta sẽ khóc lóc và nghiến răng.
vi.R: Đến ngày tận thế cũng sẽ như vậy. Các thiên sứ sẽ đến và đem những kẻ ác ra khỏi những người làm theo ý muốn của Đức Chúa Trời. \v 50 Các thiên sứ sẽ ném những kẻ ác vào ngọn lửa cháy như lò lửa. Ở đó họ sẽ khóc lóc và nghiến răng.

ko.L: 시대의 끝에도 그렇게 될 것이다. 천사들이 나와서 의인들 가운데서 악한 자들을 가려내어 \v 50 그들을 불가마 속에 던져 넣을 것이다. 거기에는 울음과 이를 가는 일이 있을 것이다.
ko.B: 이 시대의 끝에도 이와 같을 것이다. 천사들이 와서 의인들 가운데서 악한 사람들을 가려내어, \v 50 불타는 가마 속에 던져 넣을 것이다. 거기서 그들은 울며 이를 갈 것이다.
ko.R: 세상의 끝 날에도 그렇게 될 것이다. 천사들이 와서, 하나님께서 원하시는 일을 한 사람들 가운데서 악한 사람들을 가려낼 것이다. \v 50 그리고 악한 사람들을 가마처럼 뜨겁게 타는 불 속에 던져 넣을 것이다. 거기서 그들은 울며 이를 갈 것이다.

pt.L: Assim será no fim da era: os anjos sairão e separarão os maus do meio dos justos \v 50 e os lançarão na fornalha de fogo; ali haverá choro e ranger de dentes.
pt.B: Assim será o fim da era. Os anjos virão e tirarão os maus do meio dos justos, \v 50 e os lançarão na fornalha ardente. Ali as pessoas vão chorar e ranger os dentes.
pt.R: É assim que vai ser no fim do mundo. Os anjos vão chegar e separar as pessoas más das pessoas que fazem o que Deus quer. \v 50 Os anjos vão jogar as pessoas más no fogo que queima como uma fornalha. Ali elas vão chorar e ranger os dentes.

decisions.choice: the angels will separate the evil from the righteous: the final judgment
decisions.reason: As in 13:41-42, the separation is done by angels at the end, not by people now (13:29-30).

decisions.choice: the furnace of fire: as in 13:42 and Daniel 3:6
decisions.reason: The same words close both explanations.

decisions.choice: the people who do what God wants
decisions.reason: As in 13:43.

decisions.choice: the end of the world
decisions.reason: As in 13:39.

decisions.choice: "la fin de l’âge" (L); "la fin de l’âge présent" (B); "la fin du monde" (R)
decisions.reason: As at 13:39-40: Literal keeps the word, Balanced adds "présent" so that "âge" reads as an era, Readable uses the familiar phrase as the English does.

decisions.choice: utimilifu wa enzi (L); mwisho wa enzi (B); mwisho wa dunia (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek speaks of the close of the present age. "Enzi" (age, era) keeps that at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "the end of the world", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "lúc kết thúc của đời này" (L, B); "ngày tận thế" (R)
Worded as the Korean Matthew 13:39-43 at each level: "시대의 끝", "불가마", "의인"
decisions.reason: The same pictures as in the explanation of the weeds (13:39-43); Korean keeps the same words so the two endings read alike.

records.literal_gloss: Have you understood these things all?

en.L: Have you understood all these things?"
en.R: Do you understand all these things?"

fr.R: Est-ce que vous comprenez tout cela ? »

vi.L: "Các con đã hiểu tất cả những điều này chưa?"
vi.B: "Các con đã hiểu hết những điều ấy chưa?"
vi.R: "Các con có hiểu tất cả những điều này không?"

decisions.choice: no words introduce the question, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: "Jesus says to them" before the question, in many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "Jesus says to them" before the question. Without it, the question continues Jesus's speech. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: understood: grasped the meaning
decisions.reason: Understanding is what the crowds lacked (13:13-15, 19) and what the good soil has (13:23).

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Han entendido|Habéis entendido}}
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the disciples, so every plural "you" and its verb is the reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain). English has no such choice. The same throughout the passage.

vi.R: Các môn đồ trả lời: "Dạ, chúng con hiểu."

decisions.choice: Yes, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Yes, Lord, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "Lord" to the disciples' answer. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: "Dạ, hiểu" (L); "Dạ, chúng con hiểu" (B, R) for "Yes"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese answers such a question by repeating the verb, with the polite "dạ" of disciples to their teacher; Literal keeps it short. The verb "nói" has no "đã" at Literal, where Matthew uses the present.

decisions.choice: "예" for "Yes"
decisions.reason: "예" is the more formal yes, fitting the 합쇼체 the disciples use with Jesus.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τοῦτο πᾶς γραμματεὺς μαθητευθεὶς τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅστις ἐκβάλλει ἐκ τοῦ θησαυροῦ αὐτοῦ καινὰ καὶ παλαιά.

records.literal_gloss: He but said to them, Because of this every scribe having been discipled to the kingdom of the heavens like is to a man master of a house who brings out out of the treasure of him new things and old.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Because of this, every scribe who has been made a disciple for the kingdom of the heavens is like a man [who is] master of a house, who brings out of his treasure new things and old."
en.B: He told them, "That is why every scribe who has been trained as a disciple for the kingdom of heaven is like a householder who draws from his store of treasures both new things and old."
en.R: Then Jesus said to them, "So every teacher of the law who has become a follower in the kingdom of heaven is like the owner of a house. He brings out new things and old things from the place where he keeps his treasures."

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les dijo: «Por esto, todo escriba hecho discípulo para el reino de los cielos es semejante a un hombre dueño de casa, que saca de su tesoro cosas nuevas y antiguas».
es.B: Y les dijo: «Por eso, todo escriba que ha sido formado como discípulo para el reino de los cielos es como el dueño de una casa que saca de su depósito de tesoros lo nuevo y lo antiguo».
es.R: Entonces Jesús les dijo: «Por eso, todo maestro de la ley que se ha hecho seguidor en el reino de los cielos es como el dueño de una casa. Ese hombre saca cosas nuevas y cosas antiguas del lugar donde guarda sus tesoros».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « C’est pourquoi tout scribe qui a été fait disciple pour le royaume des cieux est semblable à un maître de maison qui tire de son trésor des choses nouvelles et des choses anciennes. »
fr.B: Il leur dit : « C’est pourquoi tout scribe formé comme disciple pour le royaume des cieux est semblable à un maître de maison qui tire de ses réserves des trésors nouveaux et anciens. »
fr.R: Puis Jésus leur a dit : « Ainsi, tout spécialiste de la Loi qui est devenu disciple dans le royaume des cieux ressemble au propriétaire d’une maison. Il sort de l’endroit où il garde ses trésors des choses nouvelles et des choses anciennes. »

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Kwa hiyo kila mwandishi aliyefanywa mwanafunzi kwa ajili ya ufalme wa mbinguni anafanana na mtu, mwenye nyumba, anayetoa kutoka hazina yake mambo mapya na ya zamani."
sw.B: Akawaambia, "Ndiyo maana kila mwandishi aliyefundishwa kuwa mwanafunzi kwa ajili ya ufalme wa mbinguni ni kama mwenye nyumba anayetoa katika ghala lake la hazina mambo mapya na ya zamani."
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akawaambia, "Basi, kila mwalimu wa sheria aliyekuwa mfuasi katika ufalme wa mbinguni ni kama mwenye nyumba. Yeye hutoa vitu vipya na vitu vya zamani kutoka mahali anapohifadhi hazina zake."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Vì thế, mọi thầy thông giáo đã được dạy làm môn đồ cho vương quốc thiên đàng thì giống như một người chủ nhà, là người lấy ra từ kho báu của mình những vật mới và vật cũ."
vi.B: Ngài nói với họ: "Vì vậy, mọi thầy thông giáo đã được huấn luyện làm môn đồ cho vương quốc thiên đàng thì giống như một người chủ nhà, lấy ra từ kho của mình cả những của báu mới lẫn của báu cũ."
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Vậy, mỗi thầy dạy luật nào đã trở thành môn đồ trong vương quốc thiên đàng thì giống như một người chủ nhà. Người ấy lấy ra những vật mới và những vật cũ từ nơi mình cất giữ của báu."

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "그러므로 천국을 위하여 제자가 된 율법학자는 누구나, 자기 곳간에서 새것과 옛것을 꺼내는 집주인과 같다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "그러므로 천국의 제자로 훈련받은 율법학자는 모두, 자기 곳간에서 새것과 옛것을 꺼내 오는 집주인과 같다."
ko.R: 그러자 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "그러니 율법 선생이 천국의 제자가 되면, 그는 집주인과 같다. 집주인은 자기 보물을 두는 곳에서 새것도 꺼내고 옛것도 꺼낸다."

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes disse: "Por isso, todo escriba que foi feito discípulo para o Reino dos céus é semelhante a um homem, dono de casa, que tira do seu tesouro coisas novas e velhas."
pt.B: Ele lhes disse: "Por isso, todo escriba que foi instruído como discípulo para o Reino dos céus é como um dono de casa que tira do lugar onde guarda os seus tesouros tanto coisas novas como antigas."
pt.R: Então Jesus disse a eles: "Por isso, todo mestre da Lei que se tornou seguidor no Reino dos céus é como o dono de uma casa. Ele tira coisas novas e coisas velhas do lugar onde guarda os seus tesouros."

decisions.choice: made a disciple for the kingdom: taught as a disciple, for the kingdom
alternatives: made a disciple of the kingdom
made a disciple in the kingdom
decisions.reason: The verb is passive and the phrase "the kingdom" has no preposition. It can mean trained for the kingdom, or taught about it, or made its disciple. The sense is close in each case.

decisions.choice: scribe: a teacher of the law; here one who has become Jesus's disciple
decisions.reason: Scribes were experts in the law of Moses. A scribe taught by Jesus knows both the old law and what is new in the kingdom (5:17-20).

decisions.choice: new things and old: what is new in Jesus's teaching together with the old Scriptures
decisions.reason: The householder uses both. Jesus came not to abolish the law and the prophets but to fulfill them (5:17).

decisions.choice: treasure: a storeroom, a store of valuable things
decisions.reason: The word means both the treasure and the place where it is kept.

decisions.choice: scribe (L, B); teacher of the law (R)
alternatives: expert in the law at every level
decisions.reason: The settled wording. The householder is a figure in a parable, so the pronouns for him take no deity_pronoun span, as with the bridegroom at 9:15.

decisions.choice: escriba (L, B); maestro de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "escriba" at Literal and Balanced, and at Readable what a scribe was, a teacher of the law (meaning decision m2), as the English does.

decisions.choice: "scribe" (L, B); "spécialiste de la Loi" (R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament term sheet, as the English "teacher of the law" at Readable. Readable says "disciple" where the English says "follower", as the French keeps "disciple" at every level.

decisions.choice: mwandishi (L, B); mwalimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "mwandishi" at Literal and Balanced, and at Readable what a scribe was, a teacher of the law (meaning decision m2), as the English does.

decisions.choice: "thầy thông giáo" (L, B); "thầy dạy luật" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled terms for the scribes; here a scribe who has become Jesus's disciple (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "đã được dạy làm môn đồ" (L); "đã được huấn luyện làm môn đồ" (B); "đã trở thành môn đồ" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is "to be made a disciple" (meaning decision); Vietnamese has no single verb for it, so each level uses "môn đồ" with a verb that fits its register.

decisions.choice: "율법학자" (L, B), "율법 선생" (R); "집주인"; "곳간" (L, B), "보물을 두는 곳" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Korean Matthew 7:29, 10:25 and 12:35; the treasure is a storeroom of valuable things (meaning decision).

source.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς παραβολὰς ταύτας, μετῆρεν ἐκεῖθεν.

records.literal_gloss: And it happened when finished the Jesus the parables these, he went away from there.

en.L: And it happened, when Jesus had finished these parables, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went away from there.
en.B: When Jesus had finished telling these parables, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} moved on from there.
en.R: When Jesus finished telling these parables, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left that place.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando Jesús hubo terminado estas parábolas, partió de allí.
es.B: Cuando Jesús terminó de contar estas parábolas, se marchó de allí.
es.R: Cuando Jesús terminó de contar estas parábolas, se fue de ese lugar.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand Jésus eut achevé ces paraboles, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} partit de là.
fr.B: Quand Jésus eut fini de raconter ces paraboles, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} quitta cet endroit.

sw.B: Yesu alipomaliza kusimulia mifano hii, aliondoka pale.
sw.R: Yesu alipomaliza kusimulia mifano hii, aliondoka mahali pale.

ko.R: 예수께서는 이 비유들을 다 말씀하시고 나서 그곳을 떠나셨다.

pt.L: E aconteceu que, quando Jesus terminou estas parábolas, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} partiu dali.
pt.B: Quando Jesus terminou de contar essas parábolas, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} partiu dali.
pt.R: Quando Jesus terminou de contar essas parábolas, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} foi embora daquele lugar.

decisions.choice: when Jesus had finished: the formula that closes the third long speech
decisions.reason: Matthew ends each great speech with these words (7:28; 11:1; 19:1; 26:1). This one closes the parables of chapter 13.

decisions.choice: went away: moved on, set out from there
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift and move on, used of a journey.

decisions.choice: partió, se marchó, se fue, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: English "he" takes the setting. Spanish leaves the subject pronoun out and joins some object pronouns to the verb, so there is nothing separate to capitalise; spans go only on separate pronouns and possessives ("su", "lo", "él"). Spanish therefore has fewer spans than English through the passage.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); historic presents kept at Literal
decisions.reason: As the style guide (section 3) and Mark 6: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative, the passé composé is how Readable tells a story. Speech keeps its own tenses. This holds for the rest of the chapter.

decisions.choice: "Và xảy ra là, khi ... đã nói xong" (L)
decisions.reason: The formula that closes each of Matthew's long speeches, worded as in 7:28 in the Vietnamese Matthew.

decisions.choice: "마치시자" (L)
decisions.reason: The formula that closes Jesus's long speeches is worded as the Korean Matthew 7:28.

source.text: καὶ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὴν πατρίδα αὐτοῦ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ αὐτῶν, ὥστε ἐκπλήσσεσθαι αὐτοὺς καὶ λέγειν· Πόθεν τούτῳ ἡ σοφία αὕτη καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις;

records.literal_gloss: And having come into the hometown of him he was teaching them in the synagogue of them, so that to be astonished them and to say, From where to this one the wisdom this and the miracles?

en.L: And coming into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hometown, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished and said, "Where did this [man] get this wisdom and these mighty works?
en.B: Jesus came to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hometown and began teaching the people in their synagogue. They were astounded. "Where did this man get such wisdom," they asked, "and these mighty works?
en.R: Jesus went back to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hometown, Nazareth. He taught the people in their synagogue, and they were amazed. They said, "Where did this man get such wisdom? Where did {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} get the power to do these miracles?

es.L: Y viniendo a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} tierra, les enseñaba en la sinagoga de ellos, de modo que se asombraban y decían: «¿De dónde [le vienen] a este esta sabiduría y las obras poderosas?
es.B: Jesús llegó a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo y se puso a enseñar a la gente en la sinagoga de ellos. Estaban asombrados y decían: «¿De dónde le viene a este hombre tal sabiduría, y estas obras poderosas?
es.R: Jesús volvió a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo, Nazaret. Enseñaba a la gente en la sinagoga de ellos, y todos quedaron asombrados. Decían: «¿De dónde sacó este hombre tanta sabiduría? ¿De dónde {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} viene el poder para hacer estos milagros?

fr.L: Et étant venu dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} patrie, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les enseignait dans leur synagogue, si bien qu’ils étaient frappés d’étonnement et disaient : « D’où [viennent] à celui-ci cette sagesse et ces actes de puissance ?
fr.B: Jésus se rendit dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} ville natale et se mit à enseigner les gens dans leur synagogue. Ils furent stupéfaits. « D’où cet homme tient-il cette sagesse, disaient-ils, et ces œuvres puissantes ?
fr.R: Jésus est retourné dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} ville, à Nazareth. Il a enseigné les gens dans leur synagogue, et ils étaient très étonnés. Ils disaient : « Où est-ce que cet homme a trouvé une telle sagesse ? Où a-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} trouvé la puissance de faire ces miracles ?

sw.L: Na alipokuja katika mji {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa nyumbani, alikuwa akiwafundisha katika sinagogi lao, hivi kwamba walishangaa na kusema, "Huyu [amepata] kutoka wapi hekima hii na matendo haya ya nguvu?
sw.B: Yesu alifika katika mji {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa nyumbani, akaanza kuwafundisha watu katika sinagogi lao. Wakastaajabu sana, wakasema, "Hekima kama hii imetoka wapi kwa mtu huyu, na matendo haya ya nguvu?
sw.R: Yesu alirudi katika mji {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa nyumbani, Nazareti. Akawafundisha watu katika sinagogi lao, nao wakashangaa. Wakasema, "Mtu huyu alipata wapi hekima ya namna hii? Alipata wapi nguvu ya kufanya miujiza hii?

vi.L: Và đến quê hương mình, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dạy dỗ họ trong nhà hội của họ, đến nỗi họ kinh ngạc và nói: "Người này lấy đâu ra sự khôn ngoan này và các việc quyền năng này?
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu về quê hương mình và giảng dạy dân chúng trong nhà hội của họ. Họ sửng sốt và nói: "Ông ta lấy đâu ra sự khôn ngoan và những việc quyền năng như thế?
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trở về Na-xa-rét, thị trấn nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã lớn lên. Ngài dạy dân chúng trong nhà hội của họ, và họ rất kinh ngạc. Họ nói: "Ông ta học ở đâu mà khôn ngoan như vậy? Ông ta lấy đâu ra quyền năng để làm những phép lạ này?

ko.L: 그리고 자기 고향에 가셔서 그들의 회당에서 그들을 가르치고 계셨는데, 그들이 놀라서 말했다. "이 사람이 이 지혜와 능력 있는 일들을 어디서 [얻었느냐]?
ko.B: 예수께서 고향에 가셔서 그곳 회당에서 사람들을 가르치셨다. 사람들은 크게 놀라서 말했다. "이 사람이 이런 지혜와 능력 있는 일들을 어디서 얻었을까?
ko.R: 예수께서 자라나신 마을인 나사렛으로 돌아가셨다. 그리고 그곳 회당에서 사람들을 가르치셨다. 사람들은 깜짝 놀라 말했다. "이 사람이 이런 지혜를 어디서 얻었을까? 이런 놀라운 일들을 할 수 있는 능력은 어디서 얻었을까?

pt.L: E, chegando à {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} terra natal, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os ensinava na sinagoga deles, de modo que ficavam maravilhados e diziam: "De onde este [homem] tirou esta sabedoria e estas obras poderosas?
pt.B: Jesus foi à {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} terra natal e começou a ensinar o povo na sinagoga deles. Eles ficaram assombrados. "De onde este homem tirou tanta sabedoria", perguntavam, "e essas obras poderosas?
pt.R: Jesus voltou para a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} cidade, Nazaré. Ele ensinou o povo na sinagoga de lá, e eles ficaram admirados. Eles diziam: "Onde este homem conseguiu tanta sabedoria? Onde {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} conseguiu o poder de fazer esses milagres?

decisions.choice: his hometown: Nazareth, where he grew up
decisions.reason: The word means one's native place. Jesus grew up in Nazareth (2:23) and now lived in Capernaum (4:13).

decisions.choice: mighty works: acts of power, miracles
decisions.reason: As at 11:20. They have heard of his works or seen some of them.

decisions.choice: where did this man get: the question doubts the source of his gifts
decisions.reason: "This one" sounds dismissive. The questions that follow show they cannot believe one of their own could have such gifts (13:57).

decisions.choice: Nazareth
decisions.reason: Readable names the town, known from 2:23.

decisions.choice: Where did @he get the power to do these miracles?
decisions.reason: Readable makes the second half of the question a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: las obras poderosas (L, B); milagros (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means acts of power (meaning decision m2). Literal and Balanced keep the idea of power, as the English "mighty works"; Readable says "milagros" and names the power in a separate question, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "actes de puissance" (L); "œuvres puissantes" (B); "miracles" (R)
decisions.reason: As Mark 6:2: the word is "acts of power" (m2); Literal and Balanced keep the idea of power, Readable says "miracles" as the English does.

decisions.choice: a deity_pronoun span on wake (his) only
decisions.reason: English marks "he" and "his" for the setting. Swahili carries "he" in the verb prefix, which cannot take a capital, so the span goes only on free pronouns and possessives, as in John and Mark. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English through the passage.

decisions.choice: matendo ya nguvu (L, B); miujiza (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means acts of power (meaning decision m2). Literal and Balanced keep the idea of power, as the English "mighty works"; Readable says "miujiza" and names the power in its own question, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "người này" (L); "ông ta" (B, R) in the townspeople's words, with no deity_pronoun span (13:54-56)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:2-3: the people of his hometown are astonished but do not trust him (meaning decisions), so they speak of him as "người này" or "ông ta", which are not words of reverence and take no setting, where the English has a span on "he" and "his".

decisions.choice: "việc quyền năng" (L, B); "phép lạ" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:2: works of power (meaning decision); Readable uses the plain word for miracle. "Dấu lạ" is kept for sign.

decisions.choice: The townspeople speak of Jesus as "이 사람" and "그", with no honorific, through 13:54-56
decisions.reason: They doubt the source of his gifts and are about to take offense (meaning decision); worded as the Korean Mark 6:2-3. The narrator still honours him.

decisions.choice: "능력 있는 일들" (L, B); "놀라운 일들" (R); "나사렛" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Korean Mark 6:2 and 6:5 in this parallel scene; Readable names the hometown, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: obras poderosas (L, B); milagres (R)
decisions.reason: The word means acts of power (m2). Literal and Balanced keep that with "obras poderosas", as the English keeps "mighty works"; Readable says "milagres", the everyday word, as the English Readable says "miracles". The same choice holds in 13:58.

source.text: οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τοῦ τέκτονος υἱός;

records.literal_gloss: Not this is the of the carpenter son?

en.L: Is this not the carpenter's son?
en.B: This is the carpenter's son, is it not?
en.R: This man is only the son of the carpenter!

es.L: ¿No es este el hijo del carpintero?
es.B: Este es el hijo del carpintero, ¿o no?
es.R: ¡Este no es más que el hijo del carpintero!

fr.L: Celui-ci n’est-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pas le fils du charpentier ?
fr.B: C’est bien le fils du charpentier, n’est-ce pas ?
fr.R: Ce n’est que le fils du charpentier !

sw.L: Je, huyu siye mwana wa seremala?
sw.B: Huyu ni mwana wa seremala, sivyo?
sw.R: Mtu huyu ni mwana wa seremala tu!

vi.L: Người này chẳng phải là con trai của người thợ mộc sao?
vi.B: Ông ta chẳng phải là con của ông thợ mộc sao?
vi.R: Ông ta chỉ là con của ông thợ mộc thôi mà!

ko.L: 이 사람은 그 목수의 아들이 아니냐?
ko.B: 이 사람은 그 목수의 아들이 아니냐?
ko.R: 이 사람은 그냥 목수의 아들일 뿐이다!

pt.L: Não é este o filho do carpinteiro?
pt.B: Este não é o filho do carpinteiro?
pt.R: Este homem é só o filho do carpinteiro!

decisions.choice: carpenter: a builder or craftsman in wood or stone
decisions.reason: The word covers anyone who builds, in wood most often but also in stone. The point is that they know his family as ordinary working people. Mark 6:3 calls Jesus himself the carpenter.

decisions.choice: is this not?: a question that expects "yes" and belittles him
decisions.reason: They know who he is and so refuse to accept what he does.

decisions.choice: a statement with "only"
alternatives: is this not the carpenter's son?
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes" and is meant to belittle. Readable says it as a statement and makes the tone plain with "only".

decisions.choice: "thợ mộc"
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:3: the familiar word covers the main sense of a builder or craftsman (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "목수"
decisions.reason: As the Korean Mark 6:3: the ordinary word for a builder in wood.

source.text: οὐχ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ λέγεται Μαριὰμ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωσὴφ καὶ Σίμων καὶ Ἰούδας;

records.literal_gloss: Not the mother of him is called Mary and the brothers of him James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?

en.L: Is not {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother called Mary, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?
en.B: Is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother not the woman called Mary? And are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers not James, Joseph, Simon and Judas?
en.R: We all know {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother, Mary. And we know {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers, James, Joseph, Simon and Judas.

es.L: ¿No es llamada {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre María, y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanos Santiago y José y Simón y Judas?
es.B: ¿Acaso {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre no es la que se llama María? ¿Y no son {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanos Santiago, José, Simón y Judas?
es.R: Todos conocemos a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre, María. Y conocemos a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanos: Santiago, José, Simón y Judas.

fr.L: Sa mère ne s’appelle-t-elle pas Marie, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} frères Jacques et Joseph et Simon et Jude ?
fr.B: Sa mère n’est-elle pas celle qu’on appelle Marie ? Et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} frères ne sont-ils pas Jacques, Joseph, Simon et Jude ?
fr.R: Nous connaissons tous {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère, Marie. Et nous connaissons {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} frères, Jacques, Joseph, Simon et Jude.

sw.L: Je, mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} haitwi Mariamu, na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} Yakobo na Yusufu na Simoni na Yuda?
sw.B: Je, mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} hajulikani kwa jina la Mariamu? Na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} je, si Yakobo, Yusufu, Simoni na Yuda?
sw.R: Sisi sote tunamjua mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, Mariamu. Na tunawajua ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, Yakobo, Yusufu, Simoni na Yuda.

vi.L: Mẹ của người này chẳng phải tên là Ma-ri, và anh em của người này là Gia-cơ, Giô-sép, Si-môn và Giu-đa sao?
vi.B: Mẹ ông ta chẳng phải là bà Ma-ri sao? Các anh em ông ta chẳng phải là Gia-cơ, Giô-sép, Si-môn và Giu-đa sao?
vi.R: Ai cũng biết mẹ ông ta là bà Ma-ri. Ai cũng biết các anh em của ông ta là Gia-cơ, Giô-sép, Si-môn và Giu-đa.

ko.L: 그의 어머니는 마리아라고 하지 않느냐? 그의 형제들은 야고보와 요셉과 시몬과 유다가 아니냐?
ko.B: 그의 어머니는 마리아라는 여자가 아니냐? 그의 형제들은 야고보와 요셉과 시몬과 유다가 아니냐?
ko.R: 우리는 그의 어머니 마리아를 다 안다. 그의 형제들인 야고보와 요셉과 시몬과 유다도 다 안다.

pt.L: Não se chama a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mãe Maria, e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} irmãos Tiago e José e Simão e Judas?
pt.B: A {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mãe não é a mulher chamada Maria? E os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} irmãos não são Tiago, José, Simão e Judas?
pt.R: Todos nós conhecemos a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mãe, Maria. E conhecemos os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} irmãos, Tiago, José, Simão e Judas.

decisions.choice: brothers: the ordinary word for brothers in the same family
alternatives: sons of Joseph by an earlier marriage
decisions.reason: The word normally means brothers. Christian traditions differ on whether these were sons of Mary and Joseph, sons of Joseph by an earlier marriage, or close relatives such as cousins. The text names them brothers and does not settle the question (see 1:25; 12:46).

decisions.choice: Joseph, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Joses, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read Joses, as in Mark 6:3; Joses is a short form of the same name. A few read John. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: James and Judas: two of the brothers named elsewhere
alternatives: the apostles of the same names
decisions.reason: They are not the apostles James and Judas of 10:2-4. A James, the Lord's brother, later led the church in Jerusalem (Galatians 1:19; Acts 15:13), and the letter of Jude names its writer as a brother of James (Jude 1).

decisions.choice: We all know
alternatives: Is not his mother called Mary?
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes". Readable says what the townspeople mean as a statement.

decisions.choice: "Jude"
decisions.reason: As Mark 6:3: French calls this brother of Jesus "Jude", which also keeps him apart from Judas Iscariot.

decisions.choice: ndugu zake
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" is the usual word for brothers of the same family, as the Greek word is (meaning decision m1), and like it can stretch to wider kin. "Kaka" would specify brothers, often older ones, and so settle a question the meaning decision leaves open.

decisions.choice: "anh em"; Gia-cơ, Giô-sép, Si-môn, Giu-đa
decisions.reason: "Anh em" names brothers without saying older or younger, as in Mark 6:3 and 12:46. The names are in their Protestant forms; "Giô-sép" for the Greek "Joseph", where Mark 6:3 has "Giô-sê".

decisions.choice: "형제들", not "동생들", with no gender span; "요셉"
decisions.reason: As the Korean Mark 3:31 and 6:3. The SBLGNT reads "Joseph" here (meaning decision), so Korean writes "요셉", where Mark has "요세".

source.text: καὶ αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ οὐχὶ πᾶσαι πρὸς ἡμᾶς εἰσιν;

records.literal_gloss: And the sisters of him not all with us are?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sisters, are they not all with us?
en.B: And are all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sisters not living here among us?
en.R: All {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sisters live right here in our town too.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanas, ¿no están todas con nosotros?
es.B: ¿Y no viven aquí entre nosotros todas {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanas?
es.R: Y todas {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanas viven aquí mismo, en nuestro pueblo.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} sœurs ne sont-elles pas toutes chez nous ?
fr.B: Et toutes {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} sœurs ne vivent-elles pas ici, parmi nous ?
fr.R: Et toutes {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} sœurs habitent ici, dans notre ville.

sw.L: Na dada {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, je, wote si wako pamoja nasi?
sw.B: Na dada {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} wote je, hawaishi hapa kati yetu?
sw.R: Dada {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} wote wanaishi hapa hapa katika mji wetu.

vi.L: Và các chị em gái của người này chẳng phải đều ở với chúng ta sao?
vi.B: Các chị em gái ông ta chẳng phải đều đang sống giữa chúng ta sao?
vi.R: Các chị em gái của ông ta cũng đang sống ngay trong thị trấn này với chúng ta mà!

ko.L: 그리고 그의 누이들은 모두 우리와 함께 있지 않으냐?
ko.B: 그의 누이들도 모두 여기서 우리와 함께 살고 있지 않으냐?
ko.R: 그의 누이들도 모두 우리 마을에 살고 있다.

pt.L: E as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} irmãs, não estão todas conosco?
pt.B: E todas as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} irmãs não moram aqui entre nós?
pt.R: Todas as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} irmãs também moram aqui mesmo na nossa cidade.

decisions.choice: his sisters: unnamed, but living in the town
decisions.reason: Matthew names the brothers but not the sisters. "All" shows there were at least two. They still live in Nazareth, among the people speaking.

decisions.choice: with us: living among us
decisions.reason: The point is that the family is ordinary and well known in the town.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: are they not all with us?
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes". Readable gives the answer.

records.literal_gloss: From where then to this one these things all?

en.L: Where then did this [man] get all these things?"
en.B: So where did {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} get all this?"
en.R: So where did {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} get all these things?"

es.L: ¿De dónde, pues, [le vienen] a este todas estas cosas?».
es.R: ¿De dónde sacó, entonces, todas estas cosas?».

fr.L: D’où [viennent] donc à celui-ci toutes ces choses ? »
fr.R: Alors, où a-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} trouvé tout cela ? »

sw.L: Basi huyu [amepata] wapi mambo haya yote?"
sw.R: Basi, amepata wapi mambo haya yote?"

vi.L: Vậy người này lấy đâu ra mọi điều ấy?"
vi.B: Vậy ông ta lấy đâu ra mọi điều này?"
vi.R: Vậy ông ta lấy đâu ra những điều này?"

ko.L: 그러면 이 사람이 이 모든 것을 어디서 [얻었느냐]?"
ko.B: 그런데 이 사람이 이 모든 것을 어디서 얻었단 말인가?"
ko.R: 그런데 이 사람은 이 모든 것을 어디서 얻었을까?"

pt.L: De onde, então, este [homem] tirou todas estas coisas?"
pt.B: Então de onde {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tirou tudo isso?"
pt.R: Então onde {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} conseguiu todas essas coisas?"

decisions.choice: where then: since his family is ordinary, where could this come from?
alternatives: a real search for his teacher
decisions.reason: "Then" draws the conclusion from their questions. The question leaves open the answer that his wisdom comes from God.

decisions.choice: "[얻었느냐]" (L), as in 13:54
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb ("from where to this one all these things?"); Korean needs one, which Literal brackets.

records.literal_gloss: And they were caused to stumble in him.

en.R: So they turned against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and would not accept {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y se ofendían a causa de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Así que se pusieron en contra de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} quisieron aceptar.

fr.L: Et ils se scandalisaient à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sujet.
fr.B: Et ils furent choqués à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sujet.
fr.R: Alors ils se sont fâchés contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et ils n’ont pas voulu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accepter.

vi.B: Thế là họ khó chịu và khước từ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Vì vậy, họ bực bội với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và không chịu tin nhận {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 그분에게 걸려 넘어지고 있었다.
ko.R: 그래서 그들은 예수를 언짢게 여기고 받아들이지 않았다.

pt.R: Por isso, eles se voltaram contra {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} e não {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} aceitaram.

decisions.choice: took offense: stumbled over him, so as to reject him
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 13:21 of falling away. They could not get past his ordinary family and so turned from him (11:6).

decisions.choice: turned against him and would not accept him
decisions.reason: Readable spells out that taking offense here means rejecting him.

decisions.choice: se ofendían (L); se sentían ofendidos (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is stumbling over him so as to reject him (meaning decision m1). Today "escandalizarse" is mostly shock at something improper; "ofenderse" says that they took offense at him.

decisions.choice: "vấp ngã vì" (L); "khó chịu và khước từ" (B)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 6:3: stumbling over him so as to reject him (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "걸려 넘어지다" (L); "못마땅하게 여기다" (B); "언짢게 여기고 받아들이지 않다" (R)
decisions.reason: Worded as the Korean Mark 6:3 in the parallel scene.

decisions.choice: tropeçavam
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of tripping, the same verb as in 13:21 (m1), where Portuguese also says "tropeça"; "escandalizar-se" now means to be shocked. Balanced says what it amounts to here, "se ofenderam".

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ ἔστιν προφήτης ἄτιμος εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ πατρίδι καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: The but Jesus said to them, Not is a prophet without honor except in the hometown and in the house of him.

en.L: But Jesus said to them, "A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown and in his household."
en.B: But Jesus told them, "Prophets are honored everywhere except in their own hometown and among their own family."
en.R: But Jesus said to them, "People honor a prophet everywhere except in his own town and in his own home."

es.L: Pero Jesús les dijo: «Un profeta no está sin honra, excepto en su patria y en su casa».
es.B: Pero Jesús les dijo: «A los profetas se los honra en todas partes, menos en su propio pueblo y entre su propia familia».
es.R: Pero Jesús les dijo: «La gente honra a un profeta en todas partes, menos en su propio pueblo y en su propia casa».

fr.L: Mais Jésus leur dit : « Un prophète n’est pas sans honneur, si ce n’est dans sa patrie et dans sa maison. »
fr.B: Mais Jésus leur dit : « Les prophètes sont honorés partout, sauf dans leur propre ville et dans leur propre famille. »
fr.R: Mais Jésus leur a dit : « Partout, les gens honorent un prophète, sauf dans sa propre ville et dans sa propre maison. »

sw.L: Lakini Yesu akawaambia, "Hakuna nabii asiye na heshima, ila katika mji wa kwao na katika nyumba yake."
sw.B: Lakini Yesu akawaambia, "Manabii huheshimiwa kila mahali, isipokuwa katika mji wao wenyewe na kati ya jamaa zao wenyewe."
sw.R: Lakini Yesu akawaambia, "Watu humheshimu nabii kila mahali, isipokuwa katika mji wake mwenyewe na nyumbani kwake mwenyewe."

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Một nhà tiên tri không phải là không được tôn trọng, ngoại trừ ở quê hương mình và trong nhà mình."
vi.B: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Nhà tiên tri được tôn trọng ở khắp nơi, trừ ra ở quê nhà và trong gia đình mình."
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Ở đâu người ta cũng tôn trọng một nhà tiên tri, trừ ở nơi người ấy lớn lên và trong chính gia đình người ấy."

ko.L: 그러나 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "예언자는 자기 고향과 자기 집 말고는 존경받지 못하는 곳이 없다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "예언자는 어디서나 존경을 받는다. 다만 자기 고향과 자기 가족에게서만은 존경을 받지 못한다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "사람들은 어디서나 예언자를 존경한다. 그러나 예언자가 자라난 고향과 그의 집에서는 그렇지 않다."

pt.L: Mas Jesus lhes disse: "Um profeta não fica sem honra, a não ser na sua terra e na sua casa."
pt.B: Mas Jesus lhes disse: "Os profetas são honrados em toda parte, menos na sua própria terra e na sua própria família."
pt.R: Mas Jesus disse a eles: "As pessoas honram um profeta em todo lugar, menos na cidade dele e na casa dele."

decisions.choice: a saying about prophets that Jesus applies to himself
decisions.reason: The words have the form of a proverb. By using it here, Jesus counts himself a prophet rejected by his own (compare 21:11, 46).

decisions.choice: household: his own family
decisions.reason: The word means house and so the family that lives in it.

decisions.choice: his (L, R); their (B); no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The pronoun belongs to the general saying about any prophet, so it takes no span. Balanced makes the saying plural.

decisions.choice: a positive statement: honored everywhere except
decisions.reason: The double negative is turned into a positive statement, which says the same thing more plainly, as at Mark 6:4.

decisions.choice: "mình", "người ấy" for the prophet, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: A saying about prophets in general, which Jesus applies to himself (meaning decision); worded as in Mark 6:4.

decisions.choice: "예언자"; "집" (L, R), "가족" (B)
decisions.reason: As the Korean Mark 6:4; the household is his own family (meaning decision). The saying is general, so no honorific.

source.text: καὶ οὐκ ἐποίησεν ἐκεῖ δυνάμεις πολλὰς διὰ τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And not he did there miracles many because of the unbelief of them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not do many mighty works there because of their unbelief.
en.B: Because they would not believe, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not do many mighty works there.
en.R: The people there did not believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did only a few miracles there.

es.L: Y no hizo allí muchas obras poderosas por la incredulidad de ellos.
es.B: Como no querían creer, no hizo allí muchas obras poderosas.
es.R: La gente de allí no creía en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Por eso hizo allí solo unos pocos milagros.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne fit pas là beaucoup d’actes de puissance, à cause de leur incrédulité.
fr.B: Parce qu’ils refusaient de croire, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne fit pas là beaucoup d’œuvres puissantes.
fr.R: Les gens de là-bas ne croyaient pas en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’y a fait que quelques miracles.

sw.L: Na hakufanya huko matendo ya nguvu mengi kwa ajili ya kutoamini kwao.
sw.B: Kwa sababu hawakutaka kuamini, hakufanya huko matendo mengi ya nguvu.
sw.R: Watu wa pale hawakumwamini. Kwa hiyo alifanya miujiza michache tu huko.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không làm nhiều việc quyền năng ở đó, vì sự vô tín của họ.
vi.B: Vì họ không tin, nên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không làm nhiều việc quyền năng ở đó.
vi.R: Dân chúng ở đó không tin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Vì vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chỉ làm một vài phép lạ ở đó thôi.

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 그들의 불신 때문에 거기서 능력 있는 일을 많이 하지 않으셨다.
ko.B: 그들이 믿지 않았으므로, 예수께서는 거기서 능력 있는 일을 많이 하지 않으셨다.
ko.R: 그곳 사람들은 예수를 믿지 않았다. 그래서 예수께서는 거기서 놀라운 일을 몇 가지밖에 하지 않으셨다.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} não fez ali muitas obras poderosas por causa da incredulidade deles.
pt.B: Como eles se recusavam a crer, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} não fez ali muitas obras poderosas.
pt.R: O povo dali não acreditou {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}. Por isso {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} fez só alguns milagres ali.

decisions.choice: not many mighty works because of their unbelief: they did not come to him in faith
decisions.reason: Mark 6:5 says he could do no mighty work there except heal a few sick people. Matthew says he did not do many. Throughout Matthew, healing comes to those who come to Jesus in faith (8:10, 13; 9:2, 22, 29).

decisions.choice: unbelief: refusal to trust him
decisions.reason: The noun is the opposite of faith. It sums up their response in 13:54-57.

decisions.choice: they would not believe (B); did not believe in him (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a verb, which is plainer than the noun.

decisions.choice: only a few miracles
decisions.reason: Readable turns the negative into a positive statement with the same meaning.

decisions.choice: "불신" (L); "믿지 않다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the Korean Mark 6:6: Literal keeps the noun, Balanced and Readable use the verb "믿다".
